name: National Coastal Resilience Fund
summary: Annual grants for planning, design and implementation of nature-based solutions, such as marsh, dune, reef and floodplain restoration, that reduce coastal hazard risks to communities in U.S. coastal areas while improving fish and wildlife habitat.

geography.label: Coastal areas of U.S. coastal and Great Lakes states, U.S. territories and Tribal lands

reporting: Grantees submit interim programmatic reports every 6 months (restoration implementation) or annually (planning and design), periodic fiscal reports, and a final programmatic report about 3 months after the grant ends.

deadline.text: Pre-Proposal Due Date: Tuesday, March 31, 2026 by 11:59 PM ET

deadline.quote: Pre-Proposal Due Date: Tuesday, March 31, 2026 by 11:59 PM ET

applicant_types.quote: Eligible applicants include non-profit 501(c) organizations, state and territorial government agencies, local governments, municipal governments, Tribal governments and organizations, educational institutions, or commercial (for-profit) organizations.

geography.quote: Projects must be located within the coastal areas of U.S. coastal states, including the Great Lakes states, and U.S. territories and Tribal lands.

access.quote: All application materials must be submitted online through the National Fish and Wildlife Foundation's Easygrants system.

window.quote: NOAA staff are also consulted on program priorities and goals for the fund's development, the annual call for proposal, and in proposal review

co_finance_required.quote: is not required but is encouraged to demonstrate broad support for the project, especially for larger scale and/or higher budgeted projects.

reporting.quote: We require interim programmatic reports every 6 months for Restoration Implementation projects and annually for planning and design projects.
